verses.1: Now, the day has come for Jehovah; he will divide your wealth among you.
verses.2: And I gathered all the nations together in Jerusalem for battle. The city was captured, and the houses and women were destroyed. Half of the city was lost, and most of the people could not be rescued from the city.
verses.3: And Jehovah will go out and fight against those nations, on the day of their calamity.
verses.4: And on that day, their feet stood on Mount Zateim, which is located in front of Jerusalem. Mount Zateim was split in half, with one half facing east and the other half facing west. It was a very large mountain. Half of the mountain was flat, while the other half was steep.
verses.5: And they will be destroyed, just as the mountains were destroyed. They will be destroyed because of the noise during the days of Ezra, the king of Judah. And Jehovah God will come with all His holy ones to help them.
verses.6: And on that day, there will be no more precious light or warmth.
verses.7: And one day, he would know by Jehovah whether it was day or night. And at noon, there would be light.
verses.8: And on that day, half of the people from Jerusalem would go to the eastern sea, and half would go to the western sea. This would happen suddenly and unexpectedly.
verses.9: And Jehovah will be the king over all the earth on that day. Then Jehovah will be one, and his name will also be one.
verses.10: All the land will be turned into a wasteland from the top to the bottom. Jerusalem, Ramah, and Ashdod will be destroyed. They will lie under the ruins of Binyamin, until the place where the old gates were located is restored again. From the hill of Hananel, all the way to the king’s wells.
verses.11: And they shall dwell in it. There will be no more war or violence. Jerusalem shall be settled in peace.
verses.12: And this will be the plague that Jehovah will bring upon all the nations who have sinned against Jerusalem. Their mouths will be sealed, and their eyes will be covered. Their tongues will be dumb.
verses.13: And on that day, there will be a great death among them. Each person will hold the hand of his neighbor, and their hands will be intertwined together.
verses.14: And Judah will also fight against Jerusalem. All the nations will gather around there, with gold, silver, and many other treasures.
verses.15: And so, there will be a plague of horses, mules, donkeys, and all the livestock that are kept in those farms. It will be like this plague.
verses.16: And all those who came from all the nations to Jerusalem, and who came year after year to worship the King of Heaven’s army, and to celebrate the festival of Sukkot.
verses.17: And it shall be that those who do not come from the tribes of the land to Jerusalem, in order to worship the King Jehovah and his armies, will not be allowed to enter.
verses.18: And if the people of Egypt do not come forward, and do not participate, then there will be a plague upon them. It will be a plague that Jehovah will bring upon those nations who do not come to celebrate the feast of Sukkot.
verses.19: This will be a sin of the Egyptians, and a sin of all those nations who do not celebrate the festival of Sukkot.
verses.20: On that day, the windows of the chariot would be made holy for Jehovah. The curtains in the house of Jehovah would be like scribes who write before the altar.
verses.21: And every vessel that is in Jerusalem and in Judea shall be considered holy to the Lord’s army. All the offerings will be brought there, and they will be used for purposes worthy of the Lord’s army. No one will be allowed to use those vessels in the Temple of the Lord’s army on that day.
